newsitem.title: USA: C&W takeover of Sprint impossible - Sprint's Esrey.
newsitem.headline: C&W takeover of Sprint impossible - Sprint's Esrey.

text.p: Sprint Corp. said Wednesday that a takeover of the company by Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc "could not be possible" because of agreements with European telephone companies that own pieces of Sprint.
The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that Cable and Wireless was considering a takeover bid worth at least $15 billion for Sprint, the No. 3 U.S. long-distance company.
The report also said Cable and Wireless, Britain's second-largest telephone company, has held talks with France Telecom, which owns 10 percent of Sprint, to line up support for a bid.
Industry analysts have said for some time that Sprint's Global One international telecommunications alliance with France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom would be a perfect fit for Cable and Wireless.

Sprint Chairman William Esrey, noting the company normally does not comment on rumours, said, "But in this case, a reported deal with Cable and Wireless supported by France Telecom could not be possible because of the terms of a standstill agreement Sprint has with France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom."

Like France Telecom, the German telecommunications giant owns 10 percent of Kansas City, Mo.-based Sprint. Both European companies are prohibited by the so-called standstill agreements from raising their stakes for now.
France Telecom also denied that it was in talks with Cable and Wireless about supporting a possible bid for Sprint.
But its chairman did say that France Telecom was talking with Cable and Wireless about becoming the British partner in the Global One alliance.

"Any report in an American journal about Cable and Wireless teaming up with France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom to buy Sprint is without any foundation," France Telecom Chairman Michel Bon told reporters in Paris.
"There are talks with Cable and Wireless and they centre on seeing whether the company can become the British partner for Global One."
Global One, set up early last year, offers corporations telecommunications services and carries international traffic for other telephone companies.

The Journal's report, quoting people familiar with the discussions, said Cable and Wireless has not made a formal offer to Sprint and faced several hurdles, including the standstill agreements, financing and regulatory issues.
A bid would be aimed at countering British Telecommunications Plc's planned $21 billion acquisition of MCI Communications Corp., the second-biggest U.S. long-distance company, the report said.
Esrey made his remarks at a Merrill Lynch conference and Sprint released them in a statement to the media.
Sprint stock rose $1.75 to $44.875 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
